summary: Sound stage-1 rewrite design. The fragment and nibble math, the exact bit-trick dequant, the non-spinning ticket split-K and the self-check plus fallback all hold up, and there is no rules problem. Three build fixes matter before the run: the activation slab layout (bank conflicts, and shared-memory bandwidth at NT=4), the gate/up pairing across warps in the w13 epilogue, and prepare-time warm-up of _align_small at the new BSM values.
justification: The mechanism is plausible. FINDINGS shows Marlin taking 87-95% of every small-M shape: 44.6 us at bs=1, 105.8 at bs=8, 116.0 at bs=16 and 187.6 at bs=32, which is roughly 1.2-2.2 TB/s against floors of 11.4/37.3/52.5/70.8 us. That leaves 2-3x of headroom on 60-weight loads. Checked details: (1) The m16n8k16 A fragment layout is right. Lane rows g and g+8 at k cols 2t+{0,1} and +8 give 8 nibbles per k16, so 4 steps fill one 16 B cp.async per (16x64) sub-tile, and 32 lanes x 16 B = 512 B is exactly that sub-tile. (2) The dequant is right and exact. (q&0x80008000)|((q&0x70007000)>>6) puts sign at bit 15 and exp2/man1 at bf16 bits 8..6, giving e2m1*2^-126 (code 0.5 becomes the subnormal 2^-127). The e4m3 scale times 2^119 stays below the bf16 max (448*2^119 < 2^128). The product has at most 6 significant bits, and bf16 mul/fma keep subnormals. The extraction order (nibbles 7-i and 3-i as hi/lo) matches the stated placement. (3) ldmatrix without .trans on a token-major, k-contiguous slab yields the col-major B fragment correctly. (4) Topk ids are distinct per token and BSM = 8*NT >= M, so no expert ever exceeds BSM routes. Every expert is exactly one m-block, the 'experts above BSM take 2 blocks' case cannot happen, and at bs=16/32 the weight restream that Marlin's 8/16-row blocks incur goes away. That is the real lever there. At bs=8 the blocking equals Marlin's (block 8), so any gain there is pure streaming efficiency. (5) The ticket reduce never spins, so a persistent grid of 132 has no co-residency or deadlock risk. (6) Smem is 88-136 KB with 1 CTA/SM, and 54 KB of weight per SM is in flight, about 1.9x the Little's-law need, so latency hiding is adequate. (7) Item balance: bs=1 has about 512 w13 and 512 w2 items over 132 CTAs (~97% last-wave efficiency), and bs=32 SK=1 has about 10 rounds. WEAKEST LINK: the shared activation slab. Its rows are 256 bf16 = 512 B apart, so every ldmatrix 8x8 hits the same 4 banks, an 8-way conflict, and the spec specifies no swizzle or pad. Even conflict-free, all 8 warps re-read the whole slab every stage, and the weight also round-trips through smem. Rough per-stage smem traffic at NT=4 is 128 KB slab reads + 16 KB weight in + 16 KB out + 16 KB slab in + 4 KB scales, about 180 KB, or ~1400 clk (~0.75 us). The DRAM time per 16 KB weight stage is ~0.45 us at 4.8 TB/s/132 SMs. So bs=32 is shared-memory bound at about 2.9 TB/s even when conflict-free, and far lower with 8-way conflicts. NT=2 is borderline and NT=1 is fine. That is still above Marlin's 1.8 TB/s, so M2 at bs=32 is reachable, but M3 (<=106 us) needs a swizzle (XOR the 16 B chunk index with row&7) or a 16 B row pad plus fewer redundant slab reads. Other minor points: the expected directions and the bs>=128 flat controls agree with TASK's weights and floors. The '<=6% partial traffic' claim holds for w13 (SK=4: 4 KB partial vs 64 KB item). For w2 at SK=8 it is ~11% written plus ~11% read, mostly L2-resident (about 2 MB at bs=1), so it is harmless but not 6%. The projected headline (~1.8x) assumes every M3 target is met; read the replaced-kernel rows, not the headline.
confounders: triton-map-align-on-block-m-restack (with triton-map-align-small-m-port): this change feeds _align_small new BSM values (16 at M 9-16, 32 at M 17-32, versus Marlin's 8/8/16), which changes the align kernel's Triton specialization (CAP_BLOCK/MB_BLOCK/BSM) and its 2.7-4.4 us row. That is a small, attributable effect, not a confound for the replaced-kernel milestone. Read the _align_small row separately in top_kernels.

post-expert-norm-triton-small-m: the consumer of y is unchanged and, like Marlin with is_ep, the new kernel never writes remote or sentinel rows, so behaviour is the same. Not a confound, as long as the w2 epilogue writes y at the flat route index (t*8+s) exactly where Marlin does.
marlin-block-m-two-smaller-on-postnorm: touches only num_tokens >= 128, which this hypothesis leaves byte for byte, so it is the in-run control. No interaction.
sglang-marlin-path-parity: this is the incumbent being replaced and the self-check's reference. Marlin's bank stays for M > 32 and for the fallback. No confound.
interference: No companions. This is kind: rewrite, judged on its own kernel rows against the Marlin pair plus act_and_mul per shape, and every bs>=128 shape runs master byte for byte as an in-run control. No landed hypothesis shares its launch sequence in a way that a revert would isolate: the align change is upstream and attributable in top_kernels, and the post-norm tail is unchanged. A sub-change control (for example the CUDA kernel at Marlin's BSM, or with silu unfused) would not change the stage-2 decision. The profile already separates the time per launch, and stage 2 is the natural follow-up.
rules_flags: load_inline runs nvcc/ninja subprocesses, which in principle touches the rule against starting processes. The precedent full-decode-cuda-gather-splitkv in muse_attention_decode passed the judge's pre-run check and scored, so this is covered by precedent. Keep it the same: compile in-process via torch.utils.cpp_extension, no network, no other subprocess.

The fused w13 epilogue computes silu(gate)*up from fp32 accumulators instead of rounding cache1 to bf16 first, and the stored intermediate (cache2) stays bf16 where SGLang keeps it. This is more precise and in-register, which is acceptable under the BF16-activation rule, but note it in the attempt file.

The second NVFP4 bank is a lossless permutation (round-trip assert) and stays NVFP4, which is allowed. The self-check is synthetic and untimed, and the tickets/workspace hold no input-derived state (counters reset to zero each replay). There are no host syncs: n_items is read on device and the grid is fixed. No flags.
open_questions: BUILD FIX: swizzle the activation slab (XOR the 16 B chunk index with token&7) or pad rows by 16 B. As written, ldmatrix on rows 512 B apart is an 8-way bank conflict on every B-fragment load. Also consider having warps share fewer slab reads (for example 4 warps x 32 weight rows), because at NT=4 the slab re-read by 8 warps makes the kernel shared-memory bound at about 2.9 TB/s.

BUILD FIX: the w13 tile puts gate rows [64j,64j+64) in warps 0-3 and up rows in warps 4-7, so silu(gate)*up at SK=1 (bs=32) needs a smem exchange the spec does not describe. Either interleave gate/up at 16-row granularity per warp (warp w gets gate 8 rows + up 8 rows, so one thread holds a matching pair), or stage the accumulators through smem. At SK>1 the last arriver reads all partials from global anyway.

BUILD FIX: prepare() warms _align_small only at Marlin's block_size_m (8/8/16). Add warm-up at the new BSM (16 for M 9-16, 32 for M 17-32), and run _align_self_check at those BSM values too, otherwise Triton JIT-compiles on the first timed call or capture.

'slot' is used for two things. The gather and epilogue index must be the route id = sorted_ids[pos] (x row = route/8, cache2/cache3 row = route), not the position pos in the sorted list. Sentinel means route >= M*8.
The spec says a spill is both in the FALLBACK list and 'printed, not fatal'. Pick one; not fatal is the sensible choice.

Use separate ticket arrays (or offsets) for the w13 and w2 launches, and assert both are zero after the self-check. Call cudaFuncSetAttribute(MaxDynamicSharedMemorySize) in prepare for all 6 instantiations before any capture.

Self-check coverage: add M=2 and M=12/24 (non-power-of-two M inside an NT class) to exercise partially filled slabs, and one case with local_start != 0 if the judge's bank can start elsewhere (prepare hard-codes (0, 32), so that only matters if the config varies).
Harvest note (as for splitkv): read the log tail first. 'PATH CHOSEN = MARLIN' or 'SELF-CHECK FAILED' means the run measured master, not the kernel.
